screening_decisions.reason: Randomized trial comparing surgeon feedback of patient preference reports (patient-reported goals/preferences) to usual care, with additional comparison of decision aids. This constitutes feedback of patient-reported information to healthcare professionals.

Randomized controlled trial where dentists received feedback of patients' dental anxiety scores (PROM) versus no feedback, measuring impact on patient state anxiety. Directly matches PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals.

Randomized controlled trial comparing session-by-session progress feedback (using Outcome Rating Scale, a PROM) to therapists versus no feedback, assessing therapeutic outcomes. Clear PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals.

Stepped wedge randomized trial providing continuous feedback on patient progress (likely measured via PROMs) to therapists and supervisors versus therapists only. Involves feedback of patient-reported outcomes to healthcare professionals.
Randomized controlled trial where intervention group received access to Oncokompas, which monitors HRQOL and symptoms and provides tailored feedback to patients. This is PROMs feedback to patients.
Integrated literature review, not a randomized trial comparing PROMs feedback to no feedback. Does not meet study design criterion.

Randomized controlled trial of mobile telehealth intervention including graphical and nurse-initiated feedback based on patient-reported data (symptoms, self-monitoring) versus standard care. Involves PROMs feedback to patients and/or healthcare professionals.

Randomized controlled trial where intervention group received regular completion of EORTC QLQ-C30 and HADS (PROMs) with feedback of results to physicians, versus control with no HRQL measurement. Direct PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals.

Randomized trial where identified depressed patients were either informed to their physician (feedback of depression screening results, a PROM) or not. Compares feedback versus no feedback of PROMs to healthcare professionals.
Laboratory study focusing on performance feedback of objective driving ability, not patient-reported outcomes. No PROMs feedback component.
Cluster randomized trial where physicians received feedback of patients' anxiety symptom levels (PROM) via a reporting system, versus control arm. Involves PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals.
Validation and reliability study of SF-36 via postal questionnaire, not a randomized trial comparing PROMs feedback to no feedback. No intervention.

Randomized controlled trial of internet-based intervention (Featback) including automated monitoring and feedback system based on self-reported eating disorder symptoms (PROMs) to patients, versus waiting list. PROMs feedback to patients.

Randomized controlled trial where physicians received reports summarizing patients' functional disability questionnaire responses (PROM), versus control group receiving no report. Direct PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals.

Intervention includes feedback on physiological measurements (peak flow, signal detection) rather than patient-reported outcomes. While some components involve symptom monitoring, feedback is not explicitly on PROMs.
Feasibility study of a multimodal supportive care intervention; abstract does not mention PROMs feedback or comparison of feedback versus no feedback. Unclear if PROMs feedback is involved.
Structured review (literature review), not a randomized trial. Does not meet study design criterion.
Observational study using statistical records to examine VTE risk; not a randomized trial of PROMs feedback.

Randomized controlled trial where case coordinators integrated pain assessment (PROM) and depression scale into routine coordination and sent summaries to physicians (feedback), versus usual care. Involves PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals.
Feasibility study developing and validating a psychometric tool for self-care activities; not a randomized trial comparing PROMs feedback to no feedback.
Randomized controlled trial where intervention group used Work Stress Questionnaire (PROM) with physician feedback, versus treatment as usual. Involves PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals.

Randomized controlled trial where intervention arm received monthly telephone monitoring using HADS and EORTC QLQ-C30 (PROMs) with feedback to oncology nurses for referral, versus educational materials alone. Involves PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals.
Multisite randomized clinical trial comparing feedback of Outcome Questionnaire-45.2 (PROM) results to therapists versus no feedback. Direct PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals.
Pilot randomized trial where intervention group received an app providing weekly symptom reporting (via ESAS, a PROM) and tailored feedback/information cards. Involves PROMs feedback to patients.
Cross-sectional mixed-methods study evaluating interpretability of PRO data presentation formats; not a randomized trial comparing PROMs feedback to no feedback.
Randomized clinical trial where intervention group received feedback based on a knowledge test (educational), not on patient-reported outcomes. No PROMs feedback component.
Qualitative interview study exploring GPs' opinions; not a randomized trial of PROMs feedback.
Feasibility cluster-randomized trial of a self-management programme; abstract does not describe feedback of PROMs to healthcare professionals or patients as the primary intervention.

Randomized trial comparing groups where patient and/or physician were told PRIME-MD results (psychiatric screening, a PROM) versus neither told. Involves feedback of PROMs to healthcare professionals and/or patients.

Pragmatic cluster randomized trial where intervention arm received automated interactive voice response tool providing physicians with real-time patient-reported data (side effects, satisfaction) about new medications. Involves PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals.

Randomized controlled trial comparing usual care, HRQL assessment, and HRQL assessment followed by structured interview and discussion (feedback of HRQL results, a PROM) to patients and nurses. Involves PROMs feedback.

Randomized trial where intervention arm made patient-reported cancer needs, QOL, and psychosocial information (PROMs) available to the health care team for coordinated interventions, versus standard care. Involves PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals.

Protocol for a pragmatic multi-site randomized controlled trial investigating self-monitoring and personalized feedback based on ESM self-reports (PROMs) of affect and thinking patterns. Involves PROMs feedback to patients.

Randomized controlled trial using FLARE-RA questionnaire (a PROM) to guide flare management intervention (nurse-led counseling or expedited visit), providing feedback to patients and healthcare professionals, compared to usual care. Measures flare occurrence and RA disease activity.

Abstract describes examples of PROMs use in practice and argues for wider uptake; no mention of randomization, comparison groups, or feedback intervention. Appears to be a commentary or descriptive paper, not an RCT testing PROMs feedback.
Abstract discusses PROs, challenges, framework for implementation; examples of application; not an RCT.
RCT evaluating short-term life review intervention; intervention is life review therapy, not PROMs feedback. No mention of using PROMs to provide feedback to clinicians or patients.

RCT where intervention group receives communication of depression screening results (PC-SAD and WHOQOL-Bref, both PROMs) and offer of psychiatric evaluation/treatment; control group receives no feedback for 3 months. Measures depression severity and quality of life. Fits: PROMs feedback to patients (and implicitly providers) vs no feedback.

RCT of depression care management program; intervention involves depression care manager providing algorithm-based care, but abstract does not specify use of PROMs for feedback; outcomes based on clinical interview and comorbidity index. Unclear if PROMs feedback is central.

RCT where intervention group has AEP scores (PROM for adverse effects of AEDs) made available to treating physicians; control group does not. Measures changes in AEP scores and QOLIE-31 scores. Fits: PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals vs no feedback.

RCT where intervention uses PCOMS (PROM for psychotherapy outcomes) with therapists (feedback condition); control is treatment as usual (no-feedback). Measures treatment gains, reliable change, etc. Fits: PROMs feedback to therapists and patients vs no feedback.

Cluster RCT where intervention includes 'monitoring and feedback tool' for physical activity (likely a PROM) embedded in SSP; control groups are SSP alone and usual care. Measures physical activity (could be PROM), self-efficacy, quality of life. The feedback tool provides monitoring and feedback.

RCT where intervention groups receive feedback that they endorsed more or fewer symptoms than average based on PCSQ (PROM); control group receives neutral information. Measures PCSQ symptom self-report (PROM) and neuropsychological performance. Fits: PROMs feedback to patients vs neutral information.

Cluster RCT where intervention group receives electronic PVQ with YV questions, results delivered to physicians before visit; control group receives PVQ without YV questions. Measures frequency of YV discussions. Fits: PROMs feedback (YV screening results) to healthcare professionals vs no YV feedback.

RCT where intervention arm receives QoL-monitor assessing QoL, distress, care needs; patients and HCPs receive copy of QoL overview and results shown in medical files. Control is usual care. Measures communication score, QoL, etc. Fits: PROMs feedback (QoL-monitor results) to patients and healthcare professionals vs usual care.

RCT where intervention group has SQ results (screening questionnaire for common mental disorders, a PROM) disclosed to and scored by GPs; control group blinded. Measures GPs' recognition and provision of care, conversation on psychological topics, follow-up rates. Fits: PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals vs no feedback.
Abstract describes developing a classification system for PRO measures; not an RCT.

Cluster RCT where intervention provides physicians with patients' alcohol screening results (CAGE questionnaire, a PROM for alcohol problems) and recommendations; control is usual care. Measures discussions about alcohol use and alcohol use. Fits: PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals vs usual care.
Abstract describes objectives for a systematic review on routine measurement and feedback of PROMs; not an RCT.

Title suggests feedback intervention, but abstract is truncated and provides no methodological details (no mention of randomization, control group, or PROMs). Insufficient information to confirm it meets criteria.
RCT of web-based communication tool for collaborative care; tool is for communication and coordination, not specifically for PROMs feedback. No mention of using or providing feedback of PROMs.

Cluster RCT where intervention surgeons receive peer benchmarked PROMs feedback and education; control surgeons do not. Measures postoperative OHS, HOOS, EQ-5D, complications. Fits: PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals vs no feedback.

RCT where intervention groups receive feedback regarding patient progress (likely via PROMs) to therapists; control groups do not. Measures patient outcome and number of sessions attended. Fits: feedback of patient progress (PROMs) to therapists vs control.

RCT where intervention group receives results of self-administered computerized assessment (PROQSY) of common mental disorders for GP; control groups: no additional information, or GHQ results. Measures clinical outcome via GHQ. Fits: PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals vs no feedback or alternative feedback.

RCT where intervention group discusses HRQOL results (measured by KIDSCREEN-27, a PROM) face to face with physician quarterly; control group receives care as usual. Measures HRQOL dimensions. Fits: PROMs feedback (HRQOL results) to patients and physicians vs usual care.

Cluster RCT where intervention uses STarT Back Tool (patient-reported data, i.e., PROM) to categorize LBP risk and guide treatment; control clinics receive no training. Measures back-related physical function and pain severity. Fits: PROMs feedback (via risk stratification based on patient-reported data) to healthcare professionals vs no such feedback.

RCT where intervention includes recovery-focused pre-diagnostic wellbeing assessment and counselling, diagnostic consultation with written feedback (based on assessments including WHO Wellbeing Index, EUROQOL, which are PROMs); control is treatment as usual. Measures WHO Wellbeing Index (primary) and other outcomes. Fits: feedback based on PROMs assessments to patients vs usual care.
Abstract is truncated but clearly about guidance for evaluating complex interventions; not an RCT.

RCT where intervention groups: in-person counseling (PE) and computer-generated feedback letters (CO); control: assessment only (AO). The computer-generated feedback letters are based on screening (likely PROMs for alcohol use). Measures gram alcohol per week, at-risk alcohol use, etc. Fits: PROMs feedback (via letters) vs no feedback (AO) and vs another intervention.
Protocol for an RCT investigating acceptability of different PROM administration methods; not a completed trial evaluating PROMs feedback intervention.

RCT where intervention group patients have SF-36 results (PROM) given to physicians before encounter; control group has results withheld. Measures physicians' responses about usefulness of SF-36, patients' satisfaction. Fits: PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals vs no feedback.

RCT where intervention group receives electronic screening and personalized feedback with clinician decision support; control group receives standard screening and counseling. Measures counseling receipt and risk behaviors at 3 months. Fits: PROMs feedback (personalized feedback based on screening) vs standard screening/counseling.
Realist synthesis reviewing how PROMs support communication and care; not an RCT.

RCT where intervention group patients report symptoms and preferences via tablet system, this information is processed and provided to patient and clinician; control group does not receive this. Measures congruence between reported symptoms and those addressed by clinicians. Fits: PROMs feedback (symptoms and preferences) to patients and clinicians vs no feedback.

RCT where intervention group has clinicians receive AEP (PROM for adverse effects of AEDs); control group usual care without AEP. Measures AEP scores, QOLIE-89 scores, AED modifications. Fits: PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals vs no feedback.

The study is a randomized trial comparing different components of tailored feedback messages (expectancy priming, autonomy support, exemplification) but does not include a control condition that receives no PROMs feedback. The selection criteria require a comparison between PROMs feedback and no such information.
The study is a qualitative study (interviews and thematic analysis) and not a randomised trial. The selection criteria require randomised trials.

The study is a randomised trial that compares the provision of PHQ-9 feedback to healthcare providers (intervention) vs. not providing such information (control) on patient-reported outcomes (PHQ-9 scores) and processes of care (active management of depression).

The study validates a self-assessment hearing loss screening tool (HSAQ) against audiometric evaluation. It does not involve a randomised trial comparing PROMs feedback to healthcare providers and/or patients vs. no such information.

The study examines the effect of physiology feedback (heart rate feedback) on self-reported stress and the correspondence between heart rate and self-reported stress. The feedback is not based on a patient-reported outcome measure (PROM) but on a physiological measure. Therefore, it does not meet the criterion of being PROMs feedback.

The study is a randomised trial that assesses the effect of a discharge readiness assessment (which includes a PROM: the Readiness for Hospital Discharge Scale) feedback to healthcare professionals (nurses) and/or patients (via self-assessment) on 30-day return to hospital. While the outcome (return to hospital) may be considered a process of care (healthcare utilization), the study does not measure any patient-reported health outcomes. The selection criteria require the study to measure patient-reported health outcomes and/or processes of care. Given the absence of patient-reported health outcomes and the uncertainty about whether return to hospital qualifies as a process of care in this context, we exclude. However, note we were initially unsure and considered including with low confidence, but upon reevaluation, we exclude.

The study is a randomised trial that compares an intervention (including self-tracking of symptoms and quality of life, with feedback to patients and clinicians) vs. control (usual education) on patient-reported health outcomes (depression and psychosocial functioning).

The study does not appear to be a randomised trial. It describes the use of a self-administered depression questionnaire to alert residents and then examines the impact on recognition of depression. There is no mention of randomisation or a control group.

The study is a randomised trial that compares the provision of feedback from the Outcome Questionnaire (OQ-45) and a clinical support tool (ASC) to therapists (intervention) vs. treatment-as-usual (control) on patient-reported outcomes (OQ-45 scores) and patient improvement/deterioration.
The study is a literature review and not a randomised trial. The selection criteria require randomised trials.
The study evaluates a mobile phone app-based participatory syndromic surveillance system. It does not involve a randomised trial comparing PROMs feedback vs. no feedback.

The study is a randomised trial that compares the provision of health-related quality of life (HRQL) feedback to clinicians (intervention) vs. no such feedback (control) on processes of care (number of issues discussed per encounter, management composite score) and patient-reported health outcomes (EQ-5D index).

The study is a randomised trial that compares a web-based asthma self-management system (MAP) that includes self-monitoring and feedback from a nurse case manager (thus providing PROMs feedback to patients and healthcare professionals) vs. usual care on asthma-related quality of life (a patient-reported health outcome) and asthma control (a health outcome or process of care).

The study is a randomised trial that compares three conditions: minimal screening (distress thermometer only, which provides a PROM measurement but no personalized feedback report), full screening (distress thermometer, problem checklist, and Psychological Screen for Cancer part C, plus a personalized report summarizing concerns and a report on the medical file), and triage (full screening plus optional personalized phone triage). The full screening and triage conditions provide PROMs feedback (personalized report and medical file report) to patients and healthcare professionals, while the minimal screening condition does not. The outcome is distress (a patient-reported health outcome) measured at 3-month follow-up.
The study is a debate article discussing the challenges of systematically reviewing complex interventions. It is not a randomised trial and does not evaluate PROMs feedback.

The study is a randomised trial evaluating a communication skills training program for oncologists. It does not involve PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals and/or patients or a comparison with no such information.
